title: Field guide: inference decision matrix and case narratives
author: Marcus Patel
body:
Executive summary

Purpose: This field guide equips sales engineers and account executives with a concise decision matrix, persona-focused messaging, competitor battlecards, pricing scenarios, a short pitch-deck outline, a one-page case narrative, and a prospect-oriented security FAQ. Use this during discovery, technical qualification, and board-level conversations.

1) One‑page positioning & decision matrix

Quick positioning statement:
Redwood Inference: the developer-first inference platform that makes LLMs predictable, cost-efficient, and resilient across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Decision matrix (use to recommend a deployment mode):
- Criteria: data residency, latency SLO, throughput predictability, cost sensitivity, compliance requirement, ops ownership
- Recommended mapping: Hosted API = fast time-to-value, moderate data sensitivity; Dedicated = predictable throughput & SLAs, moderate-to-high throughput; Private (VPC/on‑prem) = high compliance/data residency, customer-managed network and KMS

How to use: score each criterion 0-3 during discovery. Sum scores and pick the deployment with the highest alignment. Example: a healthcare payer with strict residency (3), high compliance (3), medium latency (2) -> Private.

2) Persona-focused value props (elevator + technical hooks)

- Platform Engineers / Infrastructure Leads:
  - Elevator: Standardize inference across orgs and reduce maintenance burden with a single API, observability, and rollout tooling.
  - Hooks: Token-level cost breakdown, autoscaling policies, canary rollouts, RBAC & VPC peering.

- ML Engineers / Model Ops:
  - Elevator: Deploy model variants, run A/B rollouts, and measure regressions with built-in evals and prompt-set quality checks.
  - Hooks: KV cache control, quantization profiles, continuous batching tuning, per-model performance profiles.

- Product Managers / Application Owners:
  - Elevator: Faster feature launches and predictable inference economics so roadmap tradeoffs are data-driven.
  - Hooks: Usage analytics, per-route cost, latency percentiles, fallback policies for degradation.

- Security / Compliance Officers:
  - Elevator: Keep sensitive inference in a Private deployment with optional on-prem packaging, KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs.
  - Hooks: Dedicated control plane, network isolation, SOC2 controls (see security FAQ).

3) Competitive brief & win themes

Summary: Most competitors trade off performance controls for simplicity or give raw infra without unified tooling. Redwood’s angles: production-first controls, unified runtime across environments, and explicit unit-economics levers.

Competitive matrix (quick reference):
| Competitor | Strength | Weakness | Redwood win themes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Major Cloud ML Endpoint | Managed infra, deep cloud integrations | High per-token cost, limited rollouts across clouds | Consistent pricing profiles, model fallbacks, lower tail latency at scale |
| Specialist Inference Vendor | High perf on-prem runtimes | Integration complexity, limited dev experience | Unified API plus on-prem option and better dev tooling |
| LLM API-first Provider | Simple developer UX, lots of models | Weak observability, limited enterprise controls | Token-level visibility, SLA & dedicated capacity offers |

Objection handling (battlecard snippets):
- Objection: "We can host ourselves cheaper."
  - Response: Show TCO comparison for 12-month horizon including ops headcount, incident MTTR, and opportunity cost of slower rollouts. Highlight quantization and batching suggestions that reduce per-token cost while preserving latency SLOs.
- Objection: "We can’t send PII to hosted services."
  - Response: Recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with strict VPC peering + KMS; walk through audit log and data flow sketches.

4) Pricing guidance: three starter scenarios

Guidance principle: pricing conversations should move from feature/value -> unit economics -> commitment. Provide simple math that non‑technical execs can digest. All numbers are example placeholders; confirm with finance before including in commercial proposals.

Scenario A — Pilot (Proof-of-Value)
- Target: 3-month pilot, < 50k tokens/day, 1 model (chat)
- Offer: Hosted Usage with starter discount (20% off list for first 3 months) + free onboarding (SE hours: 8)
- Outcome metric sellers track: Avg latency p50 < 300ms, cost-per-1k-tokens under target X

Scenario B — Platform Adoption (Mid-market)
- Target: 6–12 months, 500k–2M tokens/day, 3–5 endpoints
- Offer: Dedicated capacity reservation (monthly commitment) + 3 months free burst credits and discounted SE hours for migration
- Commercial talking points: Projected 12-month unit cost reduction vs cloud-hosted endpoints, SLA (99.9% availability), included rollouts and tracing integrations

Scenario C — Regulated Enterprise
- Target: Private deployment, on-prem or VPC, multi-region failover, encrypted-at-rest and in-flight keys
- Offer: Enterprise license (platform fee + yearly support), professional services for deployment (60–120 SE days), quarterly business reviews and extended observability retention
- Commercial talking points: Compliance package + indemnities, dedicated support SLAs, data residency guarantees

Quick pricing worksheet (talking points to quantify during demo):
1) Baseline tokens/day * 30 = monthly tokens
2) Map model variant and quantization to per-token cost (use internal price sheet)
3) Add fixed infra/commitment amortization (for Dedicated/Private)
4) Show 3 scenarios: best-effort hosted, committed Dedicated, and Private TCO including people costs

5) Pitch deck: 8-slide outline + speaker notes

Slide 1 — Title / Why now - Speaker note: One-sentence problem: inference unpredictability and hidden per-token economics.
Slide 2 — The cost & reliability trap - Show a simple chart comparing tail latency & per-token cost for common approaches.
Slide 3 — Redwood solution (single operating model) - One diagram showing Hosted / Dedicated / Private with same API.
Slide 4 — Customer outcomes (metrics) - Use bullets: 40% lower inferred per-token cost (example), 2x faster time-to-rollout, 99.9% availability for Dedicated customers.
Slide 5 — How it works (runtime + orchestration) - Call out batching, KV cache, model routing and quantization recommendations.
Slide 6 — Deployment options & security - Highlight VPC peering, KMS, audit logs, optional on-prem.
Slide 7 — Pricing & next steps - Pilot offer call-to-action, expected timeline.
Slide 8 — Appendix / proof points - Short case study + technical addenda.

6) One-page case narrative (sales use)

Title: Acme Retail — rapid personalization at scale (anonymized)
Context: Large e-commerce platform wanted real-time personalized descriptions and product recommendations at checkout.
Problem: Existing model infra had unpredictable latency spikes during peak traffic and per-month costs that scaled linearly with traffic spikes.
Solution: Redwood Dedicated with KV cache and autoscaling policies + prefix caching for high-frequency SKUs.
Results (metrics we use in conversation):
- 30% reduction in per-session inference cost (measured 90-day average)
- 45% reduction in 95th percentile latency after tuning batching and KV cache parameters
- Deployment to production in 6 weeks (including integration, A/B rollout, and QA)
Customer quote (paraphrased): "Redwood gave us predictable economics and the ability to rapidly iterate on prompts without chasing infra issues."

7) Security FAQ for prospects (short, actionable answers)

Q: "Can we keep data inside our VPC / on-prem?"
A: Yes. Private deployments support on‑prem packaging and VPC peering. We support customer‑managed KMS and HSM integrations.

Q: "How is data retained and audited?"
A: Audit logs capture request metadata (timestamp, token counts, model version, route id). For Private and Dedicated we support configurable retention windows; Hosted supports configurable shorter retention and purging pipelines.

Q: "Do you offer SOC2 / ISO evidence?"
A: Yes — Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II and an ISO readiness pad; we have a security pack for enterprise legal teams.

Q: "What encryption standards are used?"
A: TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3 in transit. AES-256 at rest. Customer-managed KMS/HSM supported for Private and Dedicated tiers.

Q: "How do you manage model drift and regression risk?"
A: Redwood Optimize integrates evals and prompt sets; we support canary rollouts and automatic regression alerts tied to predefined metrics and human review gates.

Q: "What are SLAs for Hosted vs Dedicated?"
A: Hosted: best-effort with published performance profiles. Dedicated: contractual SLA 99.9% availability and latency SLOs defined per contract.

8) Operational checklist for proof-of-value (for SEs)

Pre-demo (day -14 to -1):
- Confirm deployment recommendation (hosted/dedicated/private)
- Gather sample prompts, traffic shape, and peak QPS estimate
- Prepare baseline perf run and cost estimate

Pilot (weeks 0–12):
1) Kickoff: define success metrics and MOPs
2) Integration: API keys, network config (VPC peering if applicable), and observability hooks
3) Tune: batching, cache configuration, and quantization profile recommendations
4) Validate: run evals and compare against baseline prompt set
5) Handoff: QBR and runbook delivery
